steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and grease a small baking tin.
Mix the atta and baking powder, add the thick curd and knead gently into a soft dough. Cover and let it rest.
Mash the ripe banana with the soft butter and cinnamon into a smooth paste.
Roll the dough into a thin rectangle on a floured board, adding a little more atta if it sticks.
Spread the banana paste over it, roll it up tightly from the long side and pinch the seam closed.
Cut into slices about 3 cm wide and set them cut side up in the tin, not touching.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until lightly golden and the dough is cooked through.
Let them cool until just warm before serving.
note: A home recipe: soft curd dough with no yeast or rising, and ripe banana instead of sugar, since the NHS says to skip added sugar for under-fours. If the family buys bakery rolls instead, those are sugary, so keep them for treats; amounts are for one small roll.
